# Contractor Workforce Demand Report — July 2026
### Tech Plus | Non-Union & Open-Shop Contractor Opportunity Pipeline
*Generated by the Contractor Workforce Demand Agent. Sources cited inline; all signals verified via public web research July 2026.*

## Executive Summary

The U.S. mission-critical construction market is in the steepest labor squeeze on record. Hyperscalers have raised collective capex guidance to ~$718B (+~70% YoY), hyperscale sites are absorbing 4,000–5,000 workers each, and the construction industry is short an estimated 439,000 workers ([Dycom FQ1'27 coverage](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/261932946-dycom-ai-fiber-network-backlog-dy-stock-forecast-tradingkey)). In Texas, data centers are absorbing 45–70% of project budgets in electrical scopes and paying nearly double residential rates to poach electricians ([Texas Tribune](https://www.texastribune.org/2026/04/28/data-centers-texas-electricians-builders/)). Court filings at Stargate Abilene explicitly allege "a lack of manpower" on site ([TIME](https://time.com/article/2026/06/24/ai-data-center-stargate-abilene-texas-injuries/)).

**This is the exact market failure Tech Plus solves.** Twelve non-union / open-shop contractors below show active, verifiable workforce-demand signals. Top three immediate-action accounts:

| Rank | Company | Composite Score | Headline Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Helix Electric** | 5.0 | Hiring 400 workers for first-ever Iowa project (Cedar Rapids hyperscale DC) |
| 2 | **IES Communications** | 4.8 | 286 open roles; comms revenue +35%; building its own tech pipeline from scratch in Louisiana |
| 3 | **MMR Group** | 4.8 | Stargate Abilene electrical scope; litigation citing manpower shortfalls on a 5,000-worker site |

## Method Notes

- **Labor-status verification:** merit/open-shop status confirmed via self-description, ABC affiliation, or trade-press characterization; items marked "verify" need a confirmation pass before outreach.
- **Contacts:** named individuals are publicly associated with these companies but titles change — verify every name/title via LinkedIn before sending. No emails or direct-dials are included by design; source them via LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, or company main lines.
- **Excluded as union-signatory:** Rosendin, Cupertino Electric, Sturgeon/MYR, ArchKey — dominant DC electricals but IBEW-signatory; revisit only if they open merit divisions.
- **Refresh cadence:** re-run this agent monthly; earnings seasons (Feb/May/Aug/Nov) and state BEAD award announcements are the highest-yield windows.
